OxidizeME ME-model wrapper (Yang et al. 2019 PNAS / Palsson lab).

engine for mbp-03 / mbp-06 comparator studies. Real-solver path is
gated by upstream Python 2.7 / qMINOS install; non-strict mode lets

investigations/surrogate-modeling. Registered into build_core() so it
appears in the dashboard Registry.

investigations.name: colonies
investigations.title: Colony & Microfluidic Phenotype Quantification
investigations.description:
A phenotype-quantification investigation: measure emergent colony/microfluidic
phenotypes of whole-cell E. coli across a cost/fidelity ladder of cell models
and device geometries, using one shared phenotype panel (growth rate,
size-at-division, added length, inter-division time). It is organised as an
enabling compute foundation (Part A) that makes the science (Part B) runnable.

## Part A — Compute foundation (enabling infrastructure)

The colony composite wires N whole-cell agents (each embedding the 55-process
EcoliWCM via the bridge) into one pymunk 2D environment. Part A made it
single-machine-correct and cost-characterised:

- Daughter hydration through the engine + natural division 1->2->4 (after
  fixing mother-removal over-counting and daughter placement), coherent physics
  (jitter 0.5 -> 1e-4, coherent mass). [colonies-01, colonies-02; colony GIF]
- Per-cell wall is flat (~57 ms/tick/cell across N=1..8 on the 2026-07-26
  remote re-run @ f69f9690; pymunk is essentially free); the inner EcoliWCM is
  the whole cost, and the GIL is the single-process compute ceiling. The Ray
  protocol runs cells in separate OS processes and lifts that ceiling (~3.5x at
  N=16). [colonies-01, colonies-02]

Memory — the correction. Earlier framing (colonies-02/03) called the colony
"RAM-blocked by an unbounded native leak" and retracted the cells-per-node
budget. A focused per-process + tracemalloc hunt (2026-07-26) localized the
growth to the inner WCM's polypeptide-elongation step (82%) and mass-listener
(17%), and showed it is NOT an unbounded leak:
  - the truly-retained part is small (~0.2 MB/tick), the scipy LSODA
    integrator's rwork/iwork held per solve (equilibrium / two-component /
    charging ODEs);
  - the rest — the scary ~1.4 MB/tick on the dev mini — is allocator ARENA
    RETENTION from the elongation step's large per-tick numpy working arrays:
    freed, but macOS doesn't return the pages, so RSS climbs (invisible to
    tracemalloc). On glibc / Linux — the HPC target — the growth collapses:
    the REAL 55-process colony, built for glibc in a Linux container, grew RSS
    0.225 MB/tick vs ~1.6 on the macOS mini (7x less; end-to-end validated), and
    a synthetic reproduction of just the arena churn grew 0.017 MB/tick (0.000
    with periodic malloc_trim(0)) — so the arena-churn component is fully
    reclaimed on Linux and the residual 0.225 is the real scipy-LSODA retention.
So the "leak" was substantially a macOS measurement artifact. On the HPC
(Linux) target the colony's memory is bounded (arena churn reclaimed by glibc +
optional malloc_trim; residual ~0.2 MB/tick scipy retention is a small, named
optimization target). The compute foundation is HPC-deployable; memory is a
characterised limitation, not the story. [colonies-03; leak hunt 2026-07-26]

## Part B — Phenotype quantification (the science)

Part B reuses Part A's device geometries (mother machine, daughter machine,
free colony) and runs them across three cell-model tiers — a cheap simple
viva-munk agent, a growth-only surrogate, and the full EcoliWCM — all measured
through one shared phenotype panel. colonies-04 stands up the shared factory,
geometry builders, and phenotype extractor and validates it with simple agents.
colonies-05/06 run the two canonical viva-munk devices with simple agents
(running animation + size-at-division / birth->division-time / added-size
distributions; conclusions held for experimental data). colonies-08/09 run the
full whole-cell tier inside the device geometries. The surrogate tier and real
mother-machine-data comparison are planned follow-ons. Because the colony now
streams a bounded per-cell phenotype panel to zarr (ColonyPhenotypeRecorder),
the WCM-tier runs are length-bounded on the dev mini but unbounded on HPC.

investigations.name: multiscale-bioprocess
investigations.title: v2ecoli — Bioprocess Migration & Reactor Coupling
investigations.description:
Migrates and enhances v2ecoli for bench-scale bioprocess context, then
couples it to `vivarium-collective/pbg-bioreactordesign` for the physical
reactor side.

**Scope.** Internal v2ecoli upgrades (time-varying environment, population
aggregation, reactor coupler) plus a coupling adapter — not a reactor
wrapper built from scratch; reactor physics comes from
`pbg-bioreactordesign` consumed as a dependency. Out of scope: dynamic-FBA
as the cell side (the upstream multiscale-bioprocess roadmap's choice, see
references/expert/multiscale_bioprocess_roadmap.md); multi-cell colony
composite as the primary path (deferred); CFD / spatial-mixing;
WCM-internal mass-balance audits.

**Fed-batch is deferred.** `pbg-bioreactordesign` does not yet expose
fed-batch operations (feed schedules, dynamic volume), so until that lands
upstream or a v2ecoli-side feed Step is added, the mbp-05 Beulig benchmark
scopes to the batch portion of the dataset; the spec PR makes that scope
call explicit. Adding fed-batch is expected to be a top-priority mbp-06 gap.

**Reactor + coupling code lives in `v2ecoli/`** (planned packages
`v2ecoli.composites.ecoli_time_varying_env`,
`v2ecoli.composites.ecoli_population`,
`v2ecoli.composites.reactor_bird_coupled`); the cell-side composite stays
`v2ecoli.composites.ecoli_baseline` (single cell + Division Step).
`pbg-bioreactordesign` is added as a workspace dependency in mbp-03.

Studies, in dependency order (current `phase` shown; multi-axis status is
canonical per each study.yaml):

1. mbp-01-time-varying-environment — **Evaluate phase** — media /
   environment becomes externally driven (time-varying nutrient pool
   consumed by the existing Layer-1 Steps); plumbing + qualitative-extreme
   tests only (chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §3), with gradient-shape /
   quantitative-biology deferred to the `transport-kinetics-fidelity`
   candidate-future-study.
2. mbp-02-population-aggregation — **Evaluate phase** — aggregates per-cell
   mass into reactor-scale biomass / OD600 / cell-count via
   `cells_per_agent` representative-sampling scaling
   (chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §4; Eran's choice over literal-sum to make
   240-min batch dynamics resolvable). OD600 is cosmetic;
   `biomass_concentration_gL` is canonical.
3. mbp-03-bird-reactor-coupling — adapter to `pbg-bioreactordesign`'s
   **BiRDTransportProcess** (a transport-only sibling of
   `BiRDReactorProcess` with no internal biomass ODE; see
   `chris_feedback_2026_05_26.md` §5 for the Option-B rationale). BiRD owns
   transport physics, v2ecoli owns biomass; the keystone coupling, and the
   first impl PR to wire a real engine under the cell-side interface
   contract (`references/expert/cell_side_interface_contract.md`).
   **Cross-investigation dependency:** mbp-03 entering Build is gated on the
   upstream `pbg-bioreactor-transport-fork` PR landing in pbg-bioreactordesign
   (seeded as a candidate-future-study in mbp-06).
4. mbp-04-multigeneration-runs — sustained coupled run (≥ 3 v2ecoli
   generations); mass-balance audit; regime transition into
   substrate-limited growth.
5. mbp-05-palsson-benchmark — evaluation phase
   (`chris_feedback_2026_05_26.md` §10) rendering a structured comparison
   report (overlay panels + categorized divergences) against the Beulig
   2025 (mSystems; senior author Palsson) batch-phase prefix. Pass criteria
   are whether the comparison was executed and reported coherently, not
   whether biology matched within tolerance; divergences feed mbp-06's gap
   analysis as input.
6. mbp-06-gap-analysis — evaluation phase, not construction: walks the
   mbp-01..05 artifacts, synthesizes gaps across five axes (v2ecoli biology
   / coupling / BiRD physics / Beulig scope / methodology), and feeds the
   next investigation iteration.
7. mbp-07-millard-kinetic-metabolism — Evaluate phase — kinetic-metabolism
   (Millard 2017) drop-in cell engine (baseline_millard) + reactor coupling,
   validated against the FBA baseline and graded head-to-head against the
   Beulig WT batch prefix alongside the WCM-FBA and iML1515 arms (3-arm
   report cards).

Reconstructs a 3D structural view of the E. coli cell directly from a live
baseline whole-cell run, using the ecoli_structural composite (baseline +
an EcoliPackStep that packs the molecular state at declared simulation times).

state — for the Analysis Tools Parsimony Viewer.
